recipes.name: Japanese Soup with Tofu and Mushrooms

steps.text: Bring dashi stock to a boil in a medium saucepan; reduce heat to simmer, add mushrooms, and cook for 3 minutes.
Mix miso paste and soy sauce together in a small bowl; stir into stock along with tofu. Simmer for 5 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Japanese Soup with Tofu and Mushrooms
raw_recipe.description: This Japanese mushroom soup is a quick, healthy dish that is very popular and comforting. It's flavored with dashi, miso, shiitake mushrooms, and soy.
raw_recipe.name: Japanese Soup with Tofu and Mushrooms

recipeInstructions.text: Bring dashi stock to a boil in a medium saucepan; reduce heat to simmer, add mushrooms, and cook for 3 minutes.
Mix miso paste and soy sauce together in a small bowl; stir into stock along with tofu. Simmer for 5 minutes.

review.reviewBody: This is really good! I am currently living in Japan and couldn't figure out how to get that "authentic" miso soup taste. Dashi stock was the answer! If you want to make it even healthier and more filling, add some fresh bean sprouts! They go great in this soup.

DH doesn't like tofu but he happily ate this. i used 2 different types of organic miso, neither was named, but one was reddish the other white. i included lots of garlic, tamari, heated the onions first in the nuker to avoid extra fat (i find this a great help in indian as well) l used a mix of organic mushrooms, spinach, snow peas, green beans, a shredded carrot & of course hard organic tofu. next time i'll pop in some sprouts. i'll make this often, we both liked it. great way to restart your diet after an indulgent holiday. thanks.

Very nice! Tasted just like our local and fave Japanese restaurant miso soup with mushrooms. Made my own Doshi stock with Bonito granuals, used baby bella mushrooms instead of shiitake because of cost. Shiitake mushrooms were out of control priced....fresh and dried! Used a firm tofu and added the scallions at the end. Very good. Thanks!

Fantastic recipe! Perfect! This will be the only miso recipe I ever make. 
We don't eat unfermented soy so I used: 
Chickpea Miso instead of the soy miso and fluffy fried egg cubes instead of the tofu. I also added a bit of wakame too.
I didn't add the soy sauce as the soup is already salty and I added soba noodles, 1/4 tsp. of ginger, 1/2 tsp. of garlic. This is a delicious addition to my soup rotation for the winter.

I thought this recipe was great! I just finished cooking it. Due to the remote area that I live in, I couldn't get any Dashi stock so I substituded it with a mixture of vegie stock and chicken broth. I also added nori to it (thanks to some of the other reviews) and I found it to be an excellent addition.
I couldn't find dashi stock so I used beef broth with some sugar and soy sauce, still turned out great

This was awesome and really close to the miso soup you'd expect from your favorite sushi bar. I used a combination of mushrooms that I had on hand, and since I am a vegetarian I did not use dashi stock. Instead I used a combination of vegetable stock and water and found a great organic koji soy sauce to mix with the miso paste. My very picky friend loved it, too, so it's safe to say that it's a wonderful recipe.

This miso soup is awesome! I've made it two times now. For convenience sake instead of the dashi stock, I use 1 can of chicken broth and 11/3 cup water plus some oyster sauce. I also had the idea to add in 2 sheets of nori, to add substance and give it more nutrients. Its not as authentic but it tastes great.

Loved the flavor, though next time I would make it less like a traditional Japanese miso soup by adding a LOT more tofu and mushrooms--perhaps quadrupling it while halving the stock. I try and keep an eye on my salt intake and the stock is a big sodium bomb.
Very good, authentic sushi restaurant taste when made exactly as written. Easy. Use good quality bonito flakes to make dashi.

Soup was amazing couldn't find dashi. Used vegetable broth with chicken base . Dont really see any use for the tofu so I used asian spinach and a clear rice stick noodles.added some carrots .the green onions I added to the soup while cooking . For garnish I sliced a couple of jalapeños peppers about 1\8 inch thick it added just enough zing to it and my boys and their friend loved it.
it was a little too fishy for me. maybe i'm just not a miso soup person?

Very good soup! It was a little on the salty side, so I may use reduced sodium soy sauce the next time I make it, but my husband and I really enjoyed it. My husband is very picky when it comes to stuff like this and he said it was almost as good as the miso soup our local Chinese restaurants serve.
Oh so good. We don't eat un-fermented soy so I substituted tiny pork strips for the tofu. Thanks so much for a recipe everyone in the house loves!!

I did not like this at all. It made my house smell awful. However, I think it was probably the dashi stock I used. It was pink and weird tasting. Maybe I'm just not a miso soup type of person or maybe I didn't do something right. It just wasn't for me. I don't think I'll try this again.
Delicious! Exactly how Japanese restaurants' soups taste. Works well with any kind of mushroom.
